subject: System Design
title: DNS Caching and TTL
description: A short lesson to help you apply DNS Caching and TTL.

hook.text: If every DNS lookup queried root servers, the internet would collapse from the load.

buildup.text: DNS responses include a TTL — Time to Live — that tells resolvers how long to cache the result.

discovery.text: A TTL of 3600 means the answer is cached for one hour. No queries needed during that time.

twist.text: Low TTLs allow fast changes but increase DNS load. High TTLs reduce load but delay propagation of changes.

climax.text: DNS TTL is a trade-off between freshness and efficiency that affects every domain on the internet.

punchline.text: TTL balances fresh results with efficient caching.

quiz.question: What does DNS TTL control?
options: How long a DNS result is cached before re-querying
